Tafsir of Surah (al-Infitar)

It is Meccan.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿When the sky is split asunder﴾. Its meaning: it is cracked open (inshaqqat), and from it comes the expression "the camel's tooth split" (infatara naab al-ba'ir).
And His saying: ﴿And when the stars fall, scattering﴾, i.e., they fall down.

Wa-qawluhu: ﴿And when the seas are caused to burst forth﴾. Al-Hasan said: "They dried up."

Another (scholar) said, reported from others: "They were filled." The well-known meaning is that some of them burst into others: the sweet (water) into the brackish, and the brackish into the sweet. It was also said: "fujjirat" means they were made into one sea, by the bursting of some of them into others.

And His saying: ﴿When the graves are overturned﴾, that is: they are turned over and scattered, and the meaning is: their earth is overturned and whatever is in them of the dead is brought out.

It is related in a report (khabar) that on the Day of Resurrection the earth will cast out the fleshy pieces of its belly (afla dh kabidiha), so it will bring forth its treasures, its dead, and everything that is in it.

It is well known that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is near that the Euphrates will uncover a mountain of gold, and people will fight over it."

Al-Qaffal said: It is possible that what Allah the Exalted has mentioned of these things occurs before the Hour is established, and it is possible that it occurs after the Hour is established.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 82, verse 5:

And His saying: ﴿Every soul will know what it has sent forward and left behind﴾. That is: ﴿what it has sent forward﴾, so it did (the deeds of) action; ﴿and left behind﴾, that is: it left off from (doing) deeds. It was also said: "what it has sent forward and left behind" means: what it has done of old, in the past, and recent. And it was said concerning His saying ﴿and left behind﴾: that is, of a bad sunnah (tradition) that was practised after it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 82, verse 6:

The words of the Most High: ﴿O man, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?﴾ It is said: the verse was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira. It is also said: concerning Abu Jahl. And it is said: concerning others than them.

His words: ﴿What has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?﴾ meaning: what thing deceived you, emboldened you, and tempted you until you committed what you committed?

His words: ﴿concerning your Lord, the Generous﴾ who overlooks you, and that is in this world.

In some exegeses it is mentioned that the verse was revealed concerning Abu al-Asad, who had struck the Prophet, and Allah the Exalted did not punish him in this world. So this is the meaning of His words: ﴿concerning your Lord, the Generous﴾, who overlooked you and did not punish you in this world.

He (may Allah be pleased with him) said: We were informed by Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Junujirdi: we were informed by Abu Ishaq al-Tha'alabi: we were informed by Abu Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh: we were informed by Abu Ali ibn Habash al-Muqri': we were informed by Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl al-Muqri': we were informed by Abu Ali ibn al-Husayn: we were informed by al-Muqaddami, we were informed by Kathir ibn Hisham: we were informed by Ja'far ibn Burqan, who said: Salih ibn Mismar related to me, who said: "It reached me that the Prophet recited this verse: ﴿O man, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?﴾ and said: 'His ignorance.'"

And from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: There is none among you but that Allah will be alone with him on the Day of Resurrection, and He will say: "O son of Adam, what deceived you concerning Me? O son of Adam, what did you do in what you did? O son of Adam, how did you respond to the messengers?"

And from al-Suddi (ibn al-Mufallis), who said: "His companionship with it deceived him."

And from Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath that it was said to al-Fudayl ibn Iyad: "If Allah the Exalted were to say to you: 'What has deceived you concerning Me?', what would you say to Him?" He said: "I would say: Your curtains drawn down."

And some of them versified this:

(O concealer of sin, are you not ashamed, while Allah is with you in seclusion?)

(What deceived you concerning your Lord was His respite, and His veiling of your evil deeds for so long.)

And from Yahya ibn Mu'adh, who said: If Allah the Exalted were to say: "What has deceived you concerning your Lord?", I would say: "Your leaving me be, in the past and in the present."

And from Abu Bakr al-Warraq, who said: I would say: "The generosity of the Generous deceived me."

And from Mansur ibn Ammar, who said: I would say: "What I knew of Your past bounties deceived me."

And one of them said:

(O you who wandered in error and bewilderment, and whom His long indulgence deluded:)

(Allah gave you respite, so you defied Him, and you did not fear the aftermath of your sins.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 82, verses 7–8:

And His saying: ﴿Who created you, then proportioned you, then balanced you, in whatever form He willed﴾. ʿAṭāʾ said: He made you upright and well-proportioned, of good form. It was also said: "proportioned you" means He made equal between your two hands, your two legs, your two eyes and your two ears, and placed every part in its proper place. This is also the meaning of His saying ﴿then balanced you﴾, as mentioned by al-Kalbi and others.

It was also said: "balanced you" means He balanced your creation (ʿadl khalqika), and that is according to what we have explained.

It has been recited with the lighter form (ʿadalaka, with taškīf omitted), meaning: He turned you into whatever form He willed, of beauty or ugliness, tall or short.

In some of the strange reports it is related: "When Allah, exalted is He, wishes to create a servant, He brings forth before Him every vein that existed between him and Adam, and creates him in whatever likeness He wills, resembling whomever He wishes."

It has also been said: ﴿balanced you﴾ means: He assembled you (rakkabaka) in whatever form He willed, from the resemblance of a father, a mother, an uncle and a maternal uncle. Abu ʿAli al-Fārisi said: the meaning of ʿadalaka with the lighter form is: He made some of you equal to some of you, so you were of balanced creation, harmonious in its parts, with no disparity among them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 82, verses 10–11:

And His saying: ﴿But indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording,﴾. In some traditions it is related that the Prophet said: "Honor the noble recording angels, for they are with you, except at the time of sexual impurity (janabah) and when relieving oneself."

It has been reported from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying, the Exalted: ﴿noble and obedient﴾ that they are the angels, who are too honorable to be with the son of Adam during his privacy with his family and during his need (of relieving himself).

As for His saying: ﴿recording﴾, they are the angels who sit on the right and left of the person, recording what is for him and against him. It was also said: there is one on his right and one on his left; the one on his right records the good deeds, and the one on his left records the bad deeds. And it was said: the one on his right is trustworthy over the one on his left, and does not record except with his permission.

And in a report narrated by Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet (ﷺ): "When the servant intends a good deed, the angel records for him a good deed; then when he does it, he records for him ten good deeds. And when he intends an evil deed, nothing is recorded against him; then when he does it, it records one evil deed."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 82, verse 13:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss﴾. Concerning the report, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "They are those who were dutiful to their fathers and their sons."

The apparent meaning is that they are the obedient ones.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 82, verse 14:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, the wicked will surely be in Hellfire.﴾ It is the Fire; we seek refuge in Allah from it.

It is related in narratives that Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik performed the Hajj, and he met Abu Hazim Salama ibn Dinar, and said: "O Abu Hazim, what is the meeting with Allah like?" He said: "As for the righteous, it is like the absent one returning to his family; and as for the evildoer, it is like the runaway slave being brought back to his master." Sulayman wept, then said: "Would that I knew what our state is with Allah!" Abu Hazim said: "Present yourself to the Book of Allah, the Exalted." He said: "And upon which of it should I present myself?" He said: "Upon His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will surely be in bliss, and indeed, the wicked will surely be in Hellfire.﴾" Sulayman said: "Then where is the mercy of Allah?" He said: "Near to the doers of good."
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They will burn therein on the Day of Recompense﴾. That is, they will enter it on the Day of Resurrection.

"And His saying: ﴿And they will not be removed from it [i.e., from the Fire]﴾. That is: they will not be kept far from it."

Note on the translation: the Qur'anic phrase ﴿وَمَا هم عَنْهَا بغائبين﴾ is rendered as "And they will not be removed from it," and the bracketed gloss "[i.e., from the Fire]" is my addition to clarify the antecedent of "it." Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 82, verse 19:

And His saying: ﴿The Day when no soul will have power to do anything for another soul﴾, meaning: no soul will avail another soul in anything.

"Yawm" (Day) is in the accusative as an adverb of time (ẓarf). It has also been read in the nominative as "yawmu", and this is apparent.

And His saying: ﴿And the command on that Day belongs to Allah﴾, meaning: the command on the Day of Resurrection belongs to Allah; there is no one with Him who has any command. And Allah knows best.
